round_1_findings.finding: The newest explicit owner correction makes N a runtime parameter and defines the practical finished system as VARIABLE COGNITIVE GRID + PERSISTENT DATABASE + CLAUDE CODE. GRID10 remains usable as a benchmark configuration but has no special final authority.

Claude-derived Qwen3.5 evidence still supports dynamic context/codebook binding as a narrow model-training bottleneck: semantic readability and symbol-axis writeability are stronger than baseline dynamic binding and cross-template transfer.

The dynamic S3 binder curriculum remains useful, but owner-target architecture training must now compose that binder with process-state interpretation, persistent DB boundaries, variable-N coordination, Claude handoff/return and workspace re-entry rather than a fixed physical-GRID10 endpoint.

A corpus can accidentally learn N=10, coordinator labels or historical module names as semantic shortcuts. Training/evaluation must vary N, node identity, role allocation and state layout independently from the correct cognitive decision.

Architecture-level generalization claims require split isolation by cognitive process family and provenance ancestry, plus matched compute/token budgets across N. Aggregate accuracy at one N is insufficient.
The exact accepted 46-atom ABI identities remain a materialization gate for real model-facing dynamic-binding rows. No invented atom list is admitted by this fusion.

The owner-requested low-refusal/abliterated path must retain process cognition, ClayCode/schema/math, DB/provenance discipline and authority boundaries. Refusal suppression cannot become authority bypass.

Future Xeno harness scoring must test cognitive-process identity across grid resize, DB-vs-simulation decisions, Claude handoff/return re-entry, dynamic role reassignment and evidence-aware compression separately from final-symbol accuracy.
